content: Mifepristone should be withheld if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is an increase of more than 60 ms from baseline. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of mifepristone and glasdegib, both of which prolong the QTc interval, should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Mifepristone and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of guanfacine, haloperidol, hydroxyprogesterone caproate, ibrutinib, irinotecan, and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of histrelin and hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of hydroxyzine, idelalisib, imatinib, and infiGRATinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, increases mifepristone levels. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. If unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of itraconazole, ivabradine, ixabepilone, ketamine, ketoconazole, larotrectinib, lemborexant, leniolisib, and levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine and oral) and mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of lithium, lorlatinib, lurbinectedin, macimorelin, medroxyprogesterone, mefloquine, methadone, methylprednisolone, midazolam (intranasal), midostaurin, mirtazapine, nicardipine, nilotinib, nirogacestat, nisoldipine, olaparib, omaveloxolone, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, ondansetron, osimertinib, oxaliplatin, paclitaxel, palbociclib, palovarotene, panobinostat, pazopanib, pemigatinib, pexidartinib, pimavanserin, pirtobrutinib, pitolisant, ponatinib, pralsetinib, primaquine, quetiapine, and quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norgestrel due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and backup contraception is recommended. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
